events.title: The death of St. Bridget of Sweden
events.shortBlurb: The Swedish mystic and foundress died at Rome after years of labor for the Church…
body: Bridget's last years were spent at Rome, burdened by debts and by the enmity her plain speaking against abuses had earned. In 1372, though near seventy, she made a final pilgrimage to the Holy Land; at Bethlehem she received the vision of the Nativity — the Child lying radiant on the ground before the kneeling Virgin — that would reshape the image of Christ's birth in Western art.

She died at Rome on 23 July 1373 and was buried first at San Lorenzo in Panisperna. The next year her daughter Catherine bore her body home to Sweden, to Vadstena, the mother house of her order, where her relics are venerated to this day by Catholics and Lutherans together.

Her cause was pressed by Queen Margaret of Scandinavia, and Boniface IX canonized her on 7 October 1391; the Council of Constance confirmed the act in 1415. The return of the papacy from Avignon, for which she had pleaded so long, came four years after her death, when Gregory XI re-entered Rome in 1377, moved also by the pleading of Catherine of Siena.
